short_citation: Biber, D. 1988. Variation across Speech and Writing.
core_idea: Register can be studied through distributions of linguistic features rather than isolated examples.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Supports feature-based comparison across text types, genres, or outlets.
researcher_action: Use distributional feature counts as a bridge between corpus metrics and register interpretation.

short_citation: Biber, D. and Finegan, E. 1989. Styles of stance in English.
core_idea: Stance can be studied through lexical and grammatical marking of evidentiality and affect.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Supports richer features for hedging certainty evaluation and authorial positioning.
researcher_action: Add modal epistemic and evaluative markers to the feature list before modeling stance.

short_citation: Entman, R. M. 1993. Framing: Toward Clarification of a Fractured Paradigm.
core_idea: Frames select and make aspects of reality more salient in communication.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Gives the theoretical basis for operationalizing media frames.
researcher_action: Define frames before counting words; decide what selection salience problem definition and evaluation mean in your corpus.

short_citation: Scheufele, D. A. 1999. Framing as a Theory of Media Effects.
core_idea: Framing should distinguish media frames audience frames and frame-building processes.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Keeps the repo from treating text patterns as audience effects.
researcher_action: Separate textual frame detection from claims about reader interpretation.

short_citation: Scheufele, D. A. and Tewksbury, D. 2007. Framing Agenda Setting and Priming.
core_idea: Framing agenda setting and priming are related but analytically different media-effects models.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Helps prevent overclaiming when analyzing salience without audience data.
researcher_action: Label findings as textual framing unless the project actually measures agenda setting priming or audience effects.

short_citation: Matthes, J. and Kohring, M. 2008. The Content Analysis of Media Frames.
core_idea: Frame analysis needs reliable operational indicators rather than vague holistic coding.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Supports a codebook-driven approach to frame annotation.
researcher_action: Break each frame into observable indicators and record coder disagreements.

short_citation: Matthes, J. 2009. What's in a Frame?
core_idea: Framing studies vary widely in definition coding and validity practices.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Gives a cautionary checklist for transparent frame-analysis design.
researcher_action: Use the review as a checklist for defining frame units coding rules and validity evidence.

short_citation: Baker, P. et al. 2008. A useful methodological synergy?
core_idea: Corpus methods and close reading can be combined to study discourse patterns responsibly.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Directly models the thesis-style workflow used by this project.
researcher_action: Pair frequency collocation and KWIC outputs with close-reading examples before making discourse claims.

short_citation: Gabrielatos, C. and Baker, P. 2008. Fleeing sneaking flooding.
core_idea: Corpus evidence can expose recurring media representations while retaining qualitative interpretation.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: A strong model for studying media representations of contested social or political actors.
researcher_action: Use collocate lists and concordances to inspect repeated representational patterns.

short_citation: Baker, P. Gabrielatos, C. and McEnery, T. 2013. Sketching Muslims.
core_idea: Large press corpora can be analyzed through collocation semantic preference and discourse prosody.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Useful template for actor naming and representation analysis in news corpora.
researcher_action: Compare actor terms across time periods and inspect discourse prosodies around them.

short_citation: Baker, P. and Levon, E. 2015. Picking the right cherries?
core_idea: Corpus methods can discipline qualitative interpretation but still require careful sampling and interpretation.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Warns against cherry-picking concordance examples.
researcher_action: Report how examples were selected and connect them to aggregate corpus patterns.

short_citation: Bednarek, M. and Carr, G. 2021. Computer-assisted digital text analysis for journalism and communications research.
core_idea: Digital text analysis can support communication research when outputs remain interpretable and theory-linked.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Useful for turning scripts into communication-research workflows rather than isolated NLP demos.
researcher_action: Keep generated outputs human-readable and tie each script to a research question.

short_citation: Boumans, J. W. and Trilling, D. 2016. Taking stock of the toolkit.
core_idea: Automated content analysis tools should be assessed by task fit transparency and validation.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Supports cautious use of scripts before larger-scale NLP modeling.
researcher_action: Document whether each method is descriptive exploratory annotation-based or predictive.

short_citation: Grimmer, J. and Stewart, B. M. 2013. Text as Data.
core_idea: Automatic text methods are powerful but require validation and substantive interpretation.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: A useful guardrail for computational claims about political or media text.
researcher_action: Validate automated outputs against human interpretation and report uncertainty.

short_citation: Nicholls, T. and Culpepper, P. D. 2021. Computational Identification of Media Frames.
core_idea: Computational frame identification has strengths and weaknesses that depend on frame definitions and training data.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Helps design frame modeling after codebook and validation work exist.
researcher_action: Start with interpretable labels and gold annotations before trying predictive frame models.

short_citation: Card, D. et al. 2015. The Media Frames Corpus.
core_idea: Annotated frame corpora can connect qualitative frame theory with computational analysis.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Informs the codebook and possible supervised frame-classification extensions.
researcher_action: Use it as a design reference for label hierarchy and annotation documentation.

short_citation: Mohammad, S. et al. 2016. SemEval-2016 Task 6: Detecting Stance in Tweets.
core_idea: Stance can be modeled as a target-sensitive relation rather than simple sentiment.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Useful for separating attitudes toward China BRI ASEAN governance and risk.
researcher_action: Define stance targets explicitly before coding or modeling.

short_citation: Kucuk, D. and Can, F. 2020. Stance Detection: A Survey.
core_idea: Stance detection covers targets domains methods and evaluation settings that differ from sentiment analysis.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Provides a journal-backed map for future stance-modeling extensions.
researcher_action: Use the survey to choose target definition dataset design and evaluation measures.

short_citation: Aldayel, A. and Magdy, W. 2021. Stance detection on social media: State of the art and trends.
core_idea: Stance-detection design choices vary by target granularity domain and data source.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Helps avoid importing social-media assumptions uncritically into news analysis.
researcher_action: Adapt stance categories to news discourse instead of treating positivity as stance.

short_citation: Saha, S. et al. 2024. The Role of Stance in Assessing the Veracity of Claims.
core_idea: Stance is useful for credibility work when evidence and source relations are modeled carefully.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Connects stance to evidence evaluation without collapsing it into sentiment.
researcher_action: If adding claim analysis record who supports denies questions or reports each claim.

short_citation: Pareti, S. et al. 2016. Automatically Detecting and Attributing Indirect Quotations.
core_idea: Quotation and reported speech can be computationally detected and linked to sources.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Useful for studying how judgments are outsourced to experts institutions and documents.
researcher_action: Annotate direct and indirect reported speech before making claims about source-mediated evaluation.

short_citation: Niu, C. and Relly, J. E. 2021. News from China: News framing of the Belt and Road Initiative.
core_idea: BRI coverage can be studied as a framing problem across news sources and geopolitical contexts.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Provides a domain-specific model for BRI frame analysis.
researcher_action: Use BRI-specific frames alongside general media-frame theory.

short_citation: Flint, C. and Zhu, C. 2019. The geopolitics of connectivity cooperation and hegemonic competition.
core_idea: BRI discourse sits within tensions between connectivity cooperation and hegemonic competition.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Supports the development-platform versus strategic-contestation frame distinction.
researcher_action: Treat infrastructure and strategy as co-present frames rather than mutually exclusive categories.

short_citation: Chang, D. 2022. Sowing the Seeds of Discord.
core_idea: BRI can be interpreted through international-relations mechanisms such as wedge strategy and geopolitical alignment.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Helps contextualize strategic-contestation language in media coverage.
researcher_action: Use IR literature to interpret strategic frame labels cautiously.

short_citation: Shekhar, V. 2012. ASEAN's Response to the Rise of China.
core_idea: ASEAN states often mix engagement balancing and hedging responses toward China.
why_it_matters_for_this_repo: Useful background for interpreting cautious opportunity frames in Southeast Asian media.
researcher_action: Connect textual caution to regional hedging literature without assuming one-to-one policy reflection.
